title: Filtered PBW over an arbitrary field
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], of arbitrary characteristic, and let $L$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over $F$ [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Set $T_F(L)=\bigoplus_{m\ge0}L^{\otimes_F m}$, with multiplication by concatenation and degree-one inclusion $\iota$. Let $U(L)$ be its quotient by the two-sided ideal generated by $\iota(x)\iota(y)-\iota(y)\iota(x)-\iota([x,y])$ for all $x,y\in L$, and let $j:L\to U(L)$ be the induced linear map. Fix any ordered basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $L$, allowing $n=0$. Write $E^m=j(e_1)^{m_1}\cdots j(e_n)^{m_n}$ for $m\in\mathbf N^n$. Then $(E^m)_{m\in\mathbf N^n}$ is an $F$-basis of $U(L)$. For each $d\ge0$, let $U_{\le d}$ be the $F$-span of the products $j(x_1)\cdots j(x_r)$ with $0\le r\le d$ and $x_i\in L$, the empty product being $1$. The elements $E^m$ with $\sum_i m_i\le d$ form a basis of $U_{\le d}$. For $n=0$, $U(L)=F$ and the only basis element is $1$.

source.place: Theorem 10.36, printed p.200, and its reduction proof, pp.201--204. The reduction xy=yx+[x,y] never increases word length, giving the stated degree-filtration refinement.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-tensor-word-basis] to the given ordered basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ and identify $T_{F}(L)$ with the vector space on words in $e_1<\cdots<e_n$, multiplied by concatenation. Identify $L$ with the one-letter subspace. For $u,v\in L$ put $r(u,v)=uv-vu-[u,v]$. Bilinearity and alternation [def-wf-lie-algebra] give $r(u,v)=\sum_{i,j}u_i v_jr(e_i,e_j)$, $r(e_i,e_i)=0$ and $r(e_i,e_j)=-r(e_j,e_i)$. Thus the defining ideal $J$ is generated by $r(e_j,e_i)$ with $j>i$. As a vector subspace it is spanned by all $A r(e_j,e_i)B$, where $A,B$ are basis words: expand the left and right multipliers in the word basis; conversely this span is closed under multiplication by words on either side, hence by all tensors.

source.place: Theorem 10.36, pp.200--201, tensor word basis and the displayed spanning relations for I(g).

proof.text: Order words first by length and, for equal lengths, lexicographically using $e_1<\cdots<e_n$; write $\prec$ for this strict order. It is well founded: a descending sequence has eventually constant length, and there are only $n^q$ words of any fixed length $q$. The order is preserved on adding the same prefix and suffix. Take one rule for every occurrence of an adjacent inversion: $AabB\mapsto A(ba+[a,b])B$ for basis letters $a>b$. Every word in its right side is smaller than $AabB$: the swapped word is lexicographically smaller and bracket terms have shorter length. Let $R_{\prec w}$ be the span of contextual relations whose leading words are smaller than $w$. The span of all rule relations is $J$ by Step 1. We verify the lemma's ambiguity hypothesis in Steps 3--5.

source.place: Theorem 10.36, pp.201--202; replace the printed tensor measure with a well-founded order on words.

proof.text: Two rules at the same position agree. For disjoint positions write the word as $w=AabBuvC$, where $a>b$ and $u>v$. Put $p=ba+[a,b]$ and $q=vu+[u,v]$. The two first reducts are $ApBuvC$ and $AabBqC$; compare both with $ApBqC$. Their differences from this expression are respectively $ApB r(u,v)C$ and $A r(a,b)BqC$. Expand $p,q$ into words. Each resulting contextual relation has leading word smaller than $w$: either the other inverted pair has been swapped, or a bracket has shortened the word. Both differences therefore lie in $R_{\prec w}$. This includes adjacent disjoint pairs ($B$ empty).

source.place: Theorem 10.36, p.202, Step 4 disjoint reductions; explicit lower-relation calculation over an arbitrary field.

proof.text:
The only remaining distinct positions overlap in three consecutive letters $a>b>c$. Suppress the common prefix and suffix for the calculation. Reducing the left pair first gives $bac+[a,b]c$; swapping $ac$ and then $bc$ in its cubic term gives
$$P=cba+[b,c]a+b[a,c]+[a,b]c.$$
Reducing the right pair first gives $acb+a[b,c]$; swapping $ac$ and then $ab$ in its cubic term gives
$$Q=cba+c[a,b]+[a,c]b+a[b,c].$$
All relations used after either first reduction have leading cubic words strictly below $abc$: they are $bac,bca,acb,cab$. Thus, after restoring the same prefix and suffix, the difference between the first reducts is congruent to $P-Q$ modulo $R_{\prec w}$, where $w$ is the original contextual word.

source.place: Theorem 10.36, pp.202--203, Step 4 overlapping reductions; track the leading words explicitly.

proof.text:
In the tensor algebra the last difference is exactly
$$P-Q=r([b,c],a)+r(b,[a,c])+r([a,b],c)+[[b,c],a]+[b,[a,c]]+[[a,b],c].$$
The last three terms are zero by skew-symmetry and the Jacobi identity [def-wf-lie-algebra]: their sum is $-[a,[b,c]]-[b,[c,a]]-[c,[a,b]]$. By bilinearity as in Step 1, each of the first three terms is a linear combination of $r(e_j,e_i)$ with $j>i$. With the suppressed prefix and suffix restored, their leading words have two letters in addition to the fixed context, whereas $w$ has three; explicitly their lengths are $|A|+2+|B|<|A|+3+|B|$. They therefore belong to $R_{\prec w}$. This proves the required ambiguity condition. Repeated letters produce no extra overlap: two adjacent inversions force the strict inequalities $a>b>c$. No division or sign cancellation by $2$ is used: alternation gives $[u,v]=-[v,u]$ by expanding $[u+v,u+v]=0$, so the calculation also holds in characteristic $2$.

source.place: Theorem 10.36, p.203, Jacobi calculation in Step 4; replace mere congruence modulo the entire ideal by congruence modulo smaller relations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-triangular-linear-relations] to the word coordinate space over $F$ and the rules of Step 2. The hypotheses are the triangularity in Step 2 and the same-position, disjoint and overlapping calculations of Steps 3--5. Its relation span is $J$, so its quotient is the stated $U(L)$. An irreducible word has no adjacent inversion; its letters are therefore nondecreasing, and it is uniquely $e_1^{a_1}\cdots e_n^{a_n}$. Conversely every such word is irreducible. The lemma gives their classes as an $F$-basis, indexed exactly by $\mathbf N^n$.

source.place: Theorem 10.36, pp.203--204, Steps 5--8; agent repair using the explicit triangular linear-relations criterion.

proof.text: Fix $d\ge0$. Expanding each factor of a product of at most $d$ vectors of $L$ in the given basis expresses it as a sum of words of length at most $d$. Well-founded induction on the order in Step 2 expresses each such word in the quotient as a combination of irreducible words of length at most $d$: a reducible word equals its right side, all its terms are smaller, and their lengths never increase. Thus these irreducible words span the indicated filtered subspace. They lie in that subspace because they are themselves products of at most $d$ vectors of $L$, and are independent as a subfamily of the basis from Step 6. This proves the filtered basis clause, including $d=0$.

source.place: Theorem 10.36, p.200, reordering relation, and pp.201--202, degree-lowering reductions; bounded-degree consequence written explicitly over an arbitrary field.

proof.text: If $n=0$, there are no letters or rules and the only word is empty. The word algebra is $F$, its relation ideal is zero, and the unique exponent tuple gives the sole basis element $1$. This proves the last clause and agrees with every filtered subspace for $d\ge0$.

source.place: Theorem 10.36 and the tensor-algebra construction on p.200; empty-basis case.
